summary: Intermittent 5xx wave: connection pressure at gateway leading to runtime OOMs and elevated error rate
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (PaperTrail AI, dedicated) reports intermittent elevated 5xx rate beginning 2026-03-12 13:10 UTC. Errors observed by customer and our telemetry: a few-minute waves of 502/503/504 from the public API. Impact: end-user requests fail intermittently; customer-facing latency spikes and partial downstream retries.

Impact:
- ~3.8% 5xx rate across PaperTrail tenant during spikes (baseline ~0.02%).
- p95 latency for streaming sessions increased from 120ms to 1.4s during event windows.
- Several serving runtime pods exhibited OOM exits coincident with gateway pressure.

Environment:
- prod cluster: us-west-2
- Customer uses dedicated pool with pinned model gptx-7b-redwood-v1

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern, not deterministic):
1) Traffic burst (customer traffic + periodic batch prefetch) begins at ~T0.
2) API gateway reports elevated connection queue depth and started returning 502s when proxy-to-runtime handshakes timed out.
3) Gateway retries amplify concurrent requests to runtime; runtime batching queue grows and memory usage creeps up; a subset of worker processes hit OOM and exit.
4) Autoscaler warms additional nodes but after transient failures some requests are dropped, causing 50x-100x error amplification for affected customers for ~90-300s.

Observed logs (excerpts):
- apigw: "upstream response timeout: no response from runtime within 12s"
- apigw: "connection queue depth=318, active=284, waiting=34"
- runtime: "[worker-7] kv_cache_allocate: memory pressure high, attempting eviction"
- runtime: "fatal: allocation failed: could not allocate 900MB -> abort (OOM)"

Notes:
- Customer-side retries observed in headers (x-rt-retries=2) increased fanout.
- This appears correlated with a scheduled customer prefetch job at 13:05 UTC which increased concurrent open streaming sessions.
comments: 2026-03-12 13:25 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage and acknowledgement to customer. Advised to disable prefetch as temporary mitigation and requested request IDs and timestamps. Opened ticket with SRE.

2026-03-12 13:37 UTC - SRE channel (#sre-support): Noted connection queue spikes in us-west-2 cluster; memory usage on runtime nodes climbed steadily before OOMs. Linking dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serve/cluster-metrics?var-region=us-west-2

2026-03-12 13:50 UTC - Ravi Patel (SRE): Spun up additional warm nodes in dedicated pool and applied a transient throttling rule on gateway to limit in-flight per-tenant connections. Observed immediate reduction in new OOMs but 5xx persisted for existing inflight requests.

2026-03-12 14:05 UTC - Customer (PaperTrail AI): Confirmed disabling prefetch dramatically reduced error rate. Asked for permanent guardrails to prevent customer-level prefetch from amplifying errors.

2026-03-12 14:40 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Escalated to Runtime team to audit batching and kv-cache eviction behavior under high concurrency. Ticket assigned to runtime on-call: @runtime-oncall. See linked PR investigation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123

2026-03-13 09:15 UTC - Runtime engineer (Liam Ortiz): Reproduced memory creep locally with synthetic workload that matches customer prefetch pattern. Identified a small leak in prefix cache eviction path when many concurrent streaming sessions hit the same prefix key.

2026-03-13 11:02 UTC - Ravi Patel (SRE): Temporarily lowered gateway per-tenant in-flight limit from 512 to 128 as a safety control while runtime fix is prepared. Communicated limits to PaperTrail and CS.
2026-03-13 16:20 UTC - Customer (PaperTrail AI): Accepts temporary per-tenant limit; requests timeline for permanent fix and asks for postmortem when resolved.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Gateway connection queueing + customer retries amplifies concurrency and produces a burst of in-flight requests that exceeds runtime memory headroom for batching (confirmed by correlation with queue depth metrics).
Hypothesis 2: kv-cache eviction path has race under high-concurrency streaming leading to memory leak (local repro by runtime team validated leak).
Telemetry used: gateway connection queue depth, per-tenant in-flight counts, runtime OOM logs, pod restart counts, p95 latency by route. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serve/tenant-ops

Evidence: Node mem usage graphs show linear growth starting at spike onset; flamegraphs from a reproducer indicate retained prefix cache entries. OOM logs show allocation failure requesting ~900MB repeatedly before process exit.

Mitigations tried: 1) Disabled customer prefetch (customer-side) — reduced immediate pressure. 2) Throttled per-tenant in-flight at gateway to 128 — prevented further OOMs for now. 3) Warmed extra runtime nodes — absorbed some load but not root cause.
resolution: Workaround / short term: Gateway per-tenant in-flight limit set to 128 for affected dedicated pool; advised customer to keep prefetch disabled until fix deploys. Medium term: Runtime team merged PR to fix kv-cache eviction race (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123). Patch scheduled for canary deployment to us-west-2 on 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC with gradual rollout and observability hooks. Post-deploy actions: monitor 5xx rate and memory usage for 48h, update runbook to include automatic per-tenant throttling when queue depth > 200, and follow up with customer postmortem and compensation if SLA breach confirmed.
